Figure 3:A detailed overview ofLogTSFT data synthesis engine.Part 1 (top;Section3.1) synthesizes visual search QA pairs using the full image (I0I_{0}) along with rich visual contexts (ICI_{C}andIFI_{F}, top left) related to randomly selected target objects. After generating candidate QAs, we apply a simple heuristic filter and use a VLM-as-a-Judge to ensure quality. Part 2 (bottom;Section3.2) generates reasoning traces for the selected QA. For easy questions, we directly generate traces without tool calls (omitted here). For other questions, we first create logic chains (LML_{M}andLEL_{E}) based on two human-like strategies. A logic chain selector then chooses the more appropriate one, which is subsequently used to guide the synthesis of multi-turn reasoning traces with tool use.

Figure 4:Training dynamics after applying our simple RL procedure to the baselines andLogT-SFT.During RL, our model’s validation accuracy steadily improves, whereas other SFT baselines perform on par with, or worse than zero-RL.LogTgreatly improves the RL performance ceiling.

Figure 5:Tool call accuracy.We report tool call accuracy on V*for the base model and all post-trained models. The base model is prompted to useZoom-inin a zero-shot setting. OurLogT-SFT andLogT-RL models achieve the highestZoom-inaccuracy.

images.caption: Figure 9:An example of an exhaustive search logic chain and its corresponding tool-use reasoning trace.To locate the pink sign held by a person in the crowd, the logic chain begins by instructing the trace generator (seeSection3.2) to identify the crowd, then systematically search it from left to right. Since the trace generator successfully detects the target sign and the person in the crop returned by the thirdZoom-incall, it stops scanning the rest of the crowd and instead zooms in on the identified region to extract the final answer.

Figure 15:Qualitative case study comparing model responses to a V*question between baseline models andLogT-RL.We show the generated reasoning traces, includingZoom-incalls, for both baseline models andLogT-RL.
While Qwen2.5-VL-7B-RL,Pixel Reasoner-RL, andChain-of-Focus-RL produce the correct final answer, their responses contain hallucinations or self-contradictions. The remaining baselines make erroneousZoom-incalls and ultimately produce incorrect answers.
In contrast,LogT-RL follows a coherent and consistent reasoning chain: it first identifies the front cabin of the truck, then locates the tissue box, and finally answers the question correctly without hallucinations.
